sections.overview: The blue shark is a wide-ranging oceanic shark in the family Carcharhinidae.
sections.identification: Its streamlined body has a cobalt-blue back, pale sides and a white underside; the snout is long and narrow, and the pectoral fins are notably long.
sections.habitat: It lives in tropical, subtropical and warm-temperate waters across the world’s oceans.
sections.diet: Its mainly pelagic diet includes fishes and squid, alongside other prey when available.
sections.behavior: It undertakes long seasonal migrations and may travel alone or in groups often segregated by sex and size.
sections.reproduction: It is viviparous, and reproductive characteristics vary among ocean basins.
sections.ecology: As a pelagic predator feeding high in the marine food web, it can connect distant ocean regions through its migrations.
sections.conservation: The CMS account reports a global IUCN category of Near Threatened and a Mediterranean category of Critically Endangered; fishing, including bycatch, is a major pressure.
